profiles.title: Whole-body orientation
profiles.orientation: Begin with the assembled reference body, then choose a region for detailed, directional dissection.
limitations: Skin, fascia and most joint connective tissues are not included; vascular coverage is a selected segment subset.
Whole-body stages compare systems; they are not a single anatomical depth sequence.
Neural coverage is partial and no complete spinal cord is supplied.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Musculoskeletal frame
stages.description: Set organs and neural entries aside; retain the skeleton and available muscles.
stages.inspect: Compare the regional muscle envelopes before opening a regional explorer.

stages.title: Organ window
stages.description: Remove the body wall and skeleton from view to expose the supplied organ surfaces.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the position of organs. Internal organ layers are not segmented.

stages.title: Neural subset
stages.description: Show the brain, selected cranial/orbital nerves and central-canal representation only.
stages.inspect: The thin central canal is not the spinal cord. Peripheral limb nerves are absent.

stages.title: Skeletal framework
stages.description: Hide soft tissues to inspect the available bones. Joint surfaces remain source geometry, not a simulated joint.
stages.inspect: Use the remaining bones as orientation landmarks, then step back to restore the preceding view.

stages.title: Vascular relationships
stages.description: Set the soft tissues aside to inspect selected arteries and veins against the bones. Gaps in the source vessel tree are not reconstructed.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the source vessel segments with nearby bones. Red denotes arteries and blue denotes veins—not oxygenation. Branch continuity and calibre are not independently reviewed.

stages.title: Connective-tissue relationships
stages.description: Inspect the available discs, cartilages, ligaments, membranes or tendons with their bony context. This is not a complete joint dissection.
stages.inspect: Check the available surfaces and their neighbouring bones. Most capsules, fascia, tendons and ligaments are still missing.

profiles.title: Shoulder & arm dissection
profiles.orientation: Posterior orientation exposes the cuff as the deltoid parts are removed. Anterior rotation reveals subscapularis and the anterior arm.
limitations: Capsule, labrum, bursae and brachial plexus are not segmented.
Named muscle heads remain separate source parts; no incision or tissue reflection is simulated.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove the deltoid
stages.description: Set all available deltoid parts aside to expose the rotator-cuff surfaces.
stages.inspect: Compare supraspinatus and infraspinatus around the scapular spine.

stages.title: Expose the deep arm
stages.description: Also remove biceps heads and the long/lateral triceps heads. Brachialis and the medial triceps heads remain.
stages.inspect: Rotate around the humerus to inspect the anterior and posterior surfaces.

stages.title: Cuff study
stages.description: Restrict the view to cuff muscles and the skeletal framework.
stages.inspect: Use anterior and posterior views together; one view cannot expose the whole cuff.

stages.title: Skeletal framework
stages.description: Hide soft tissues to inspect the available bones. Joint surfaces remain source geometry, not a simulated joint.
stages.inspect: Use the remaining bones as orientation landmarks, then step back to restore the preceding view.

stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the source vessel segments with nearby bones. Red denotes arteries and blue denotes veins—not oxygenation. Branch continuity and calibre are not independently reviewed.

stages.title: Shoulder vascular detail
stages.description: Compare the available axillary, scapular and thoraco-acromial source segments with the shoulder bones.
stages.inspect: Separate the display gently, then return to zero to judge the source relationships. The brachial plexus is absent; branching, attachments and vessel calibre remain unreviewed.

profiles.title: Forearm layers & compartments
profiles.orientation: Anterior views favour the flexor side; posterior views favour the extensor side. The radius and ulna remain orientation landmarks.
limitations: Retinacula, intermuscular septa and forearm nerves are not supplied. Vessel segments do not form a complete tree.
Source muscle heads may extend across the elbow; tendons are not always independent objects.

stages.title: Remove superficial flexors
stages.description: Remove the available pronator-teres heads, wrist flexors and palmaris longus.
stages.inspect: Inspect flexor digitorum superficialis before proceeding to the deep group.

stages.title: Expose deep flexors
stages.description: Remove flexor digitorum superficialis as well.
stages.inspect: Compare the long finger/thumb flexors with distal pronator quadratus.

stages.title: Expose deep extensors
stages.description: Also remove the superficial extensor group and brachioradialis.
stages.inspect: Follow the supplied deep extensor surfaces without treating this as a complete tendon atlas.

rule.pattern: flexor digitorum profundus|flexor pollicis longus|pronator quadratus|supinator|abductor pollicis longus|extensor pollicis|extensor indicis

profiles.title: Intrinsic hand dissection
profiles.orientation: Explore the thenar and hypothenar groups around the metacarpals. Use rotation to compare palmar and dorsal relationships.
limitations: Lumbricals, palmar interossei and dorsal interossei are available as source groups per hand, not individually numbered muscles.
Both flexor-pollicis-brevis entries are quarantined for a source laterality discrepancy.

Wrist flexor retinacula are available. Palmar aponeurosis, extensor retinacula, tendon sheaths and digital nerves remain absent. Arterial source numbers are retained, not validated textbook branch counts.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove outer intrinsic muscles
stages.description: Remove abductor pollicis brevis, abductor digiti minimi and flexor digiti minimi brevis.

hide.pattern: abductor pollicis brevis|abductor digiti minimi|flexor digiti minimi brevis

stages.inspect: The deeper opponens muscles remain; this is not a complete palmar-layer reconstruction.

stages.title: Adductor pollicis study
stages.description: Keep the supplied adductor-pollicis heads with the bones.
stages.inspect: Compare the two source heads and their relationship to the metacarpals.

stages.title: Skeletal framework

stages.title: Between the metacarpals
stages.description: Set other muscles aside to inspect the supplied palmar and dorsal interosseous groups.
stages.inspect: Each highlighted set is one selectable source group, not an individual numbered muscle.

stages.title: Retinaculum & carpal arch
stages.description: Keep only the carpal bones and supplied flexor retinacula. Finger bones and overlying muscles are set aside.
stages.inspect: Choose a side, then rotate around the arch or hide the retinaculum. This is a roof-and-bone study, not a complete carpal tunnel: the median nerve is absent.

stages.title: Palmar arches & metacarpal vessels
stages.description: Compare the supplied superficial arches and metacarpal arteries with deep arches, metacarpal bones and wrist flexor retinacula.
stages.inspect: Set a retinaculum or bone aside and Undo to restore it. Source surfaces do not establish a complete arch or a safe dissection plane. Use a single-side view for a closer comparison.

stages.title: Common & proper digital arteries
stages.description: Expose the common and proper palmar digital source branches with arterial arches, without bones or muscle surfaces.
stages.inspect: Frame a small branch, isolate it or compare it with the group. Source numbering is unvalidated; the two hands have unequal supplied proper-branch subsets. Focus-only practice excludes the arch context.

stages.title: Thumb & index arterial detail
stages.description: Study princeps pollicis and radialis indicis beside first/second metacarpals and thumb/index proximal phalanges.
stages.inspect: Hide a bone or fade other entries to trace the supplied surface, then Undo. Each arterial source contains two components; no missing segment is bridged or renamed.

stages.title: Hand arterial detail exposed
stages.description: An exposed comparison of all twenty-six new hand arterial identities and the existing deep arches.
stages.inspect: Switch sides, select and frame individual arteries, or arrange the entries for source-name practice. Explode and tray translations are study aids, not physiological movement, surgical planes or proof of patent connections.

stages.title: Palmar venous & arterial arches
stages.description: Compare the four supplied palmar venous arch sources with arterial arches and wrist flexor retinacula.
stages.inspect: Switch to one hand, remove a retinaculum and Undo to restore it. Blue and red identify veins and arteries, not depth, oxygenation or proven continuity. Source depth relationships require review.

stages.title: Dorsal hand venous networks
stages.description: View the source-labelled dorsal venous networks against the metacarpal bones, without overlying muscle surfaces.
stages.inspect: Select and frame one network; set a bone aside or fade context. Each network remains one source identity, not a complete map of independently dissectible veins. Focus-only practice excludes the bones.

stages.title: Palmar & finger vein segments
stages.description: Expose the supplied metacarpal and index, middle and ring digital vein groups with venous arch context.
stages.inspect: Use a single-side view to select small segments, or separate them for source-name practice. Little-finger groups are withheld for extent review; no missing thumb, common digital vein or nerve surface is fabricated.

stages.title: Hand arteries & veins exposed
stages.description: Compare fourteen venous source identities with the twenty-eight supplied hand arterial entries, without bones or muscles.
stages.inspect: Select an artery or vein, isolate it, fade the others or use reversible separation. Red means artery and blue means vein, not oxygenation. Focus-only practice asks about the venous targets; absent connections are not bridged.

profiles.title: Hip & thigh dissection
profiles.orientation: Start anteriorly for quadriceps; rotate posteriorly for the gluteal region and hamstrings. Compartment views are alternatives to the guided peel.
limitations: Femoral/sciatic nerves, fascia lata and the hip capsule are not segmented; vessels are a selected subset.
Named biceps-femoris heads are selectable source components, not simulated cut ends.

stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove the outer muscle set
stages.description: Remove sartorius, tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus.
stages.inspect: Compare the anterior thigh with the posterior hip after changing the camera direction.

stages.title: Expose vastus intermedius
stages.description: Remove rectus femoris to reveal the deeper quadriceps surface.
stages.inspect: Inspect vastus intermedius against the femur, with the other vasti retained.

stages.title: Expose the deeper adductors
stages.description: Also remove gracilis, adductor longus and pectineus.
stages.inspect: Compare the retained adductors; this view does not show their neurovascular supply.

stages.title: Expose the deep hip group
stages.description: Also remove gluteus medius to uncover gluteus minimus.
stages.inspect: Inspect the short hip rotators from several angles.

stages.title: Skeletal framework

stages.title: Lateral thigh & iliotibial tract
stages.description: Compare the source tracts with the available tensor fasciae latae, gluteus maximus, hip bones and femora.
stages.inspect: Use the matching left/right view after choosing a side. Hide a muscle to expose the tract; use Knee & leg for the tibial context. Exploded positions are illustrative, not attachment measurements.

focuses.title: Lateral thigh & iliotibial tract
focuses.description: Compare the source tracts with the available tensor fasciae latae, gluteus maximus, hip bones and femora.
focuses.inspect: Use the matching left/right view after choosing a side. Hide a muscle to expose the tract; use Knee & leg for the tibial context. Exploded positions are illustrative, not attachment measurements.

profiles.title: Lower-leg dissection
profiles.orientation: The guided sequence opens the posterior calf. Separate compartment views show the anterior, lateral and deep posterior groups.
limitations: Crural fascia, compartment septa and peripheral nerves are absent; the selected vessels have unreviewed continuity.
Paired Achilles tendon and interosseous-membrane surfaces are available. Subtendons and knee-ligament dissection remain absent.

stages.inspect: Soleus remains after the overlying gastrocnemius heads are hidden.

stages.title: Open the deep posterior group

stages.inspect: Inspect the deep posterior muscles while rotating around the tibia and fibula.

profiles.title: Plantar-foot layers
profiles.orientation: Rotate to look at the sole. The four-layer convention guides removal of the available plantar muscles; missing members remain explicitly absent.
limitations: Long plantar ligaments are included; plantar aponeurosis, plantar plates, other major ligaments and digital nerves remain absent.
Dorsal interossei and some intrinsic foot muscles are missing.
The source uses flexor accessorius for quadratus plantae.

stages.inspect: Inspect the available second-layer muscles from the plantar surface.

stages.title: Remove plantar layer 2
stages.description: Also remove flexor accessorius and the foot lumbricals.
stages.inspect: The available third-layer muscles remain.

stages.title: Remove plantar layer 3
stages.description: Also remove the supplied short hallux flexor, hallux adductor and flexor digiti minimi brevis.

profiles.title: Chest-wall & organ exposure
profiles.orientation: Progress from the pectoral region to the rib cage, then open an educational window onto the organs.
limitations: Sternal parts and costal cartilages 1–7 are included. The eighth–tenth costal cartilage coverage remains incomplete.
Pleura, pericardium and valves are not independently segmented. Selected coronary vessels are now separately selectable.
Intercostal layers are compound meshes and cannot be removed rib-space by rib-space.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove pectoralis major
stages.description: Remove the available pectoralis-major surfaces.
stages.inspect: Compare pectoralis minor with the chest-wall surface.

stages.title: Expose deeper chest wall
stages.description: Also remove pectoralis minor and the external intercostal mesh.
stages.inspect: Internal and innermost intercostal source meshes remain.

stages.title: Open the chest window
stages.description: Hide ribs and wall muscles; retain organs and diaphragm.
stages.inspect: This is visibility removal, not a thoracotomy simulation.

stages.title: Central thoracic study
stages.description: Set both lungs aside to expose the supplied central structures.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the heart, airway and esophagus. Internal chambers are not shown.

stages.title: Central airway window
stages.description: Remove the lung aggregates and chest muscles to inspect the trachea and source-labelled main bronchial segments.
stages.inspect: These are source-defined exterior surfaces, not a bronchoscopic lumen or a validated segmental-airway tree. Bronchial boundaries and relative lengths require review.

stages.title: Short rib-elevator sets
stages.description: Inspect the source-labelled breves with the thoracic bones available in this region; lungs and superficial muscles are set aside.
stages.inspect: Use Thorax for the ribs and Spine & back for vertebral context. Individual rib attachments remain unvalidated. Longi alternatives are withheld rather than overlaid.

stages.title: Bronchial arteries & airway
stages.description: Expose two bronchial arterial source identities beside the trachea, main bronchi and aortic context, with lungs and heart removed.
stages.inspect: Set the airway aside or fade other structures to inspect a small vessel, then Undo. The variant-labelled artery remains a variant, not a normal-anatomy template. Surface proximity does not prove an attachment or patent connection.

stages.title: Oesophagus & arterial branches
stages.description: A four-entry window for the oesophagus, descending thoracic aorta and two oesophageal arterial source identities.
stages.inspect: Remove the oesophagus for an exposed arterial comparison and Undo to restore its source position. The grouped branch surface remains one selectable entry; the model does not establish branch continuity or complete supply.

stages.title: Thoracic small arteries exposed
stages.description: Compare four supplied bronchial and oesophageal arterial identities with only aortic context; airway and organ surfaces are hidden.
stages.inspect: Frame a single target, separate the group or use focus-only identification practice. Explode and arrangement are educational translations, not surgical dissection or physiological motion. Missing vessels are not reconstructed.

focuses.title: Short rib-elevator sets
focuses.description: Inspect the source-labelled breves with the thoracic bones available in this region; lungs and superficial muscles are set aside.
focuses.inspect: Use Thorax for the ribs and Spine & back for vertebral context. Individual rib attachments remain unvalidated. Longi alternatives are withheld rather than overlaid.

focuses.title: Bronchial arteries & airway
focuses.description: Expose two bronchial arterial source identities beside the trachea, main bronchi and aortic context, with lungs and heart removed.
focuses.inspect: Set the airway aside or fade other structures to inspect a small vessel, then Undo. The variant-labelled artery remains a variant, not a normal-anatomy template. Surface proximity does not prove an attachment or patent connection.

focuses.title: Oesophagus & arterial branches
focuses.description: A four-entry window for the oesophagus, descending thoracic aorta and two oesophageal arterial source identities.
focuses.inspect: Remove the oesophagus for an exposed arterial comparison and Undo to restore its source position. The grouped branch surface remains one selectable entry; the model does not establish branch continuity or complete supply.

profiles.title: Abdominal organ windows
profiles.orientation: The supplied wall is incomplete, so these stages are named exposure windows rather than a complete abdominal-wall dissection.
limitations: Rectus abdominis, internal oblique and transversus abdominis are not included.
Three selected mesenteric surfaces and named vascular segments are available; peritoneal leaves, roots, organ-internal layers and complete vessel/nerve/lymphatic networks are not established.
Organ removal is an educational visibility change, not a surgical sequence.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove the available wall
stages.description: Set the external obliques aside. Deeper wall layers are not available.
stages.inspect: Inspect the available organs without assuming absent wall tissue has been dissected.

stages.title: Visceral-organ window
stages.description: Hide remaining skeletal and muscular context.
stages.inspect: Rotate to inspect organ relationships in the reference model.

stages.title: Posterior-organ window
stages.description: Set the overlying digestive organs aside to study the pancreas, kidneys and adrenal glands.
stages.inspect: These surfaces retain the shared source coordinates; they are not patient-specific.

stages.title: Bowel junction window
stages.description: Set unrelated organs, bones and muscles aside to compare the two bowel aggregates with their separately selectable junction.
stages.inspect: Select the junction to isolate or frame it. Removing either bowel aggregate does not remove the junction. This is an exposure window, not a surgical dissection sequence.

stages.title: Anterior midline junction
stages.description: Remove the viscera to examine the linea alba and the available external-oblique surfaces.
stages.inspect: Inspect the narrow midline surface, then fade or hide the external oblique. This is not a complete abdominal-wall dissection; rectus muscles, sheath layers and internal aponeuroses are not shown here.

stages.title: Mesenteric surfaces & bowel
stages.description: Keep the three supplied mesenteric surfaces with bowel context; hide a bowel aggregate to inspect the surface behind it.
stages.inspect: Set the bowel aside, then restore it with Undo to compare source relationships. Removing a surface is an educational visibility change, not peritoneal dissection.

stages.title: Mesenteric vessels exposed
stages.description: Remove bowel and mesenteric surfaces to compare available arterial and venous segments with existing major-vessel context.
stages.inspect: Select and isolate an individual segment, or use the separate arterial and venous windows. Red and blue distinguish source artery/vein labels, not oxygenation. Gaps are not bridged with invented vessels.

stages.title: Colic & appendicular arteries
stages.description: Compare the admitted bowel arterial segments without overlying organs or veins.
stages.inspect: Frame a small branch for closer study. Continuity, territories and variant branching require review; the held ileal alternatives are not displayed.

stages.title: Mesenteric venous drainage
stages.description: Isolate the available mesenteric veins with the existing hepatic portal-vein source context.
stages.inspect: These are reference surfaces, not contrast enhancement, flow or a verified continuous drainage model.

stages.title: Appendix, mesoappendix & artery
stages.description: A close four-structure window without the large bowel aggregates obscuring the supplied appendiceal context.
stages.inspect: Hide or fade the mesoappendix to inspect the available artery and appendix. The junction surface is context, not a complete cecum. Attachments and surgical planes remain unvalidated.

stages.title: Pancreas & supplied vessel detail
stages.description: Keep the pancreas with eleven newly supplied vessel identities in a close study window.
stages.inspect: Set the pancreas aside, compare the exposed vessels, then Undo to restore its source position. Explode and tray views are educational translations, not dissection planes or physiological movement.

stages.title: Pancreaticoduodenal arteries exposed
stages.description: Remove organ surfaces and veins to inspect the supplied superior/inferior arterial branches and gastroduodenal trunk.
stages.inspect: Frame an individual branch or compare the target group with the existing hepatic and mesenteric arterial context. These disconnected surfaces do not prove arcade continuity, normal origins or surgical safety.

stages.title: Pancreatic body & tail vessels
stages.description: Compare four source-labelled arterial segments with the pancreas and splenic-artery context.
stages.inspect: Hide the pancreas or fade other structures to inspect a small artery. Near-touching source surfaces are not proof of an anastomosis; no branch has been extended or welded to a neighbour.

stages.title: Pancreaticoduodenal venous context
stages.description: Inspect the three-component vein group with pancreas, superior mesenteric and hepatic portal-vein context.
stages.inspect: Set aside the pancreas for an exposed venous view. One grouped label covers all three source components; individual drainage connections and missing branches remain unvalidated.

focuses.title: Anterior midline junction
focuses.description: Remove the viscera to examine the linea alba and the available external-oblique surfaces.
focuses.inspect: Inspect the narrow midline surface, then fade or hide the external oblique. This is not a complete abdominal-wall dissection; rectus muscles, sheath layers and internal aponeuroses are not shown here.

focuses.title: Mesenteric surfaces & bowel
focuses.description: Keep the three supplied mesenteric surfaces with bowel context; hide a bowel aggregate to inspect the surface behind it.
focuses.inspect: Set the bowel aside, then restore it with Undo to compare source relationships. Removing a surface is an educational visibility change, not peritoneal dissection.

profiles.title: Pelvic & gluteal exposure
profiles.orientation: Posterior stages expose the gluteal layers. The organ window shows only the supplied bladder, not a complete pelvic-organ set.
limitations: Levator-ani candidates are held for source adjudication; pelvic fascia and pelvic plexuses remain absent. The limited male reproductive subset includes prostate, testes, epididymides and seminal vesicles.
Coccygeus and the source-labelled superficial perineal muscle do not constitute a complete pelvic floor.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove gluteus maximus
stages.description: Open the outer gluteal surface.
stages.inspect: Inspect the retained muscles against the pelvic bones.

stages.title: Expose the deep gluteal group
stages.description: Also remove gluteus medius.
stages.inspect: The source model has no sciatic nerve to reveal in this region.

stages.title: Pelvic muscle & bladder window
stages.description: Set hip-region muscles and bones aside to display the available pelvic entries.
stages.inspect: Do not interpret this sparse window as a complete pelvic-floor or pelvic-organ model.

stages.title: Skeletal framework
stages.description: Hide soft tissues to inspect the available bones. Joint surfaces remain source geometry, not a simulated joint.
stages.inspect: Use the remaining bones as orientation landmarks, then step back to restore the preceding view.

stages.title: Vascular relationships
stages.description: Set the soft tissues aside to inspect selected arteries and veins against the bones. Gaps in the source vessel tree are not reconstructed.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the source vessel segments with nearby bones. Red denotes arteries and blue denotes veins—not oxygenation. Branch continuity and calibre are not independently reviewed.

stages.title: Pelvic organ subset
stages.description: Inspect bladder, ureter surfaces, rectum and the limited male reproductive subset.
stages.inspect: Compare the source positions; do not infer a complete pelvic floor, organ-wall layering, sphincters or reproductive tract.

profiles.title: Neck & cranial windows
profiles.orientation: The neck sequence removes selected superficial muscles. Separate cranial windows bypass the skull to expose the supplied neural subset.
limitations: Facial coverage is incomplete; meninges and most cranial nerves are absent. Selected neck and intracranial vessel segments are available.
Compound eyeballs are included, but no full orbital-layer, cranial-base or neck-fascia dissection is supplied.
Cranial windows hide bone; they do not cut a skull flap.
Deep-brain entries are unvalidated source surfaces. Colours identify study groups, not histology or MRI signal. The two-component choroid-plexus and mammillary records remain grouped across sides.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove platysma
stages.description: Set the available platysma surfaces aside.
stages.inspect: Use the neck muscles and hyoid as orientation landmarks.

stages.title: Expose deeper neck muscles
stages.description: Also remove sternocleidomastoid.
stages.inspect: Inspect the retained neck muscles and available vessel segments; fascial spaces and complete neurovascular anatomy remain absent.

stages.title: Cranial neural window
stages.description: Hide bones and muscles to expose the brain and available nerve branches.
stages.inspect: This is a limited cranial/orbital subset, not all cranial nerves.

stages.title: Orbital anatomy subset
stages.description: Set the brain aside; retain the compound eyeballs, available orbital nerves and extraocular muscles.
stages.inspect: Eyeballs are compound surfaces, not an ocular-layer dissection. Inspect the incomplete nerve and muscle subset around them.

stages.title: Skeletal framework
stages.description: Hide soft tissues to inspect the available bones. Joint surfaces remain source geometry, not a simulated joint.
stages.inspect: Use the remaining bones as orientation landmarks, then step back to restore the preceding view.

stages.title: Vascular relationships
stages.description: Set the soft tissues aside to inspect selected arteries and veins against the bones. Gaps in the source vessel tree are not reconstructed.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the source vessel segments with nearby bones. Red denotes arteries and blue denotes veins—not oxygenation. Branch continuity and calibre are not independently reviewed.

stages.title: Connective-tissue relationships
stages.description: Inspect the available discs, cartilages, ligaments, membranes or tendons with their bony context. This is not a complete joint dissection.
stages.inspect: Check the available surfaces and their neighbouring bones. Most capsules, fascia, tendons and ligaments are still missing.

stages.title: Salivary & lacrimal glands
stages.description: Inspect the supplied submandibular, sublingual and lacrimal glands with the bones.
stages.inspect: Parotid glands and complete duct anatomy are not supplied by this window.

stages.title: Deep-brain overview
stages.description: Hide the skull and the existing brain aggregate to expose the supplied deep-brain structures. Colours distinguish study groups, not MRI signal or actual tissue colour.
stages.inspect: Compare the paired source surfaces and midline structures. Ghost removed tissues can restore the outer reference context; it may obscure small structures.

stages.title: Basal nuclei & thalami
stages.description: Study the supplied caudate, putamen, pallidal and thalamic surfaces without overlying cortex or skull.
stages.inspect: Compare putamen and pallidum, then rotate towards the thalami. Internal capsule, individual thalamic nuclei and the complete basal-ganglia circuit are not separately shown.

stages.title: Limbic & commissural detail
stages.description: Inspect selected limbic and commissural source surfaces with the outer brain hidden.
stages.inspect: Compare the callosal arch, fornix and mammillary surfaces. This is a spatial selection, not a complete limbic circuit or a tractography reconstruction.

stages.title: Teeth & jaws
stages.description: A close dental window with 28 individually selectable source teeth, the mandible and maxillae. The rest of the skull and head are set aside.
stages.inspect: Teeth are in the Organs system, not Bones. Hide or fade a jaw to inspect root surfaces. Third molars, gingiva and periodontal tissues are absent; this is not a certified occlusal model.

stages.title: Upper tooth surfaces
stages.description: The 14 supplied upper teeth alone, viewed from below. Bone and lower teeth are removed for access to the chewing surfaces.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the source crown and root surfaces; select any tooth for its full source name. Explode is illustrative separation, not orthodontic movement. No tooth numbering, occlusion or internal tissues have been validated.

stages.title: Lower tooth surfaces
stages.description: The 14 supplied lower teeth alone, viewed from above. Bone and upper teeth are removed for access to the chewing surfaces.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare the source crown and root surfaces; select any tooth for its full source name. Explode is illustrative separation, not orthodontic movement. No tooth numbering, occlusion or internal tissues have been validated.

stages.title: Orbital rings & rectus muscles
stages.description: The two source rings, four rectus muscles on each side and eyeballs, without the enclosing skull or brain.
stages.inspect: Choose a side and inspect from behind; hide the eyeball or a rectus muscle when needed. Do not infer a complete nerve-passage map, attachment footprint or surgical corridor.

stages.title: Superior oblique & trochlea
stages.description: A small orbital window with the superior-oblique muscles, their source-labelled trochleae and the eyeballs.
stages.inspect: Choose a side, then rotate or hide the eyeball. The source muscle is not independently segmented into belly and tendon; pulley contact and continuity need review. Explode separates objects, not tissue attachments.

stages.title: Epiglottis & laryngeal framework
stages.description: A close six-structure window for the epiglottis, hyoid, thyroid/cricoid cartilages and two source ligaments.
stages.inspect: Remove one framework surface at a time and use Undo to compare the epiglottis in place. This is static visibility dissection, not a moving or clinically validated airway model.

focuses.title: Deep-brain overview
focuses.description: Hide the skull and the existing brain aggregate to expose the supplied deep-brain structures. Colours distinguish study groups, not MRI signal or actual tissue colour.
focuses.inspect: Compare the paired source surfaces and midline structures. Ghost removed tissues can restore the outer reference context; it may obscure small structures.

focuses.inspect: Select each body to compare its identity and position. Optic and auditory radiations are not supplied by this view.

focuses.title: Choroid plexus & fornix
focuses.description: Show the paired cerebral choroid-plexus source group with selected nearby reference structures.
focuses.inspect: The empty spaces are not a validated ventricular lumen. This view does not show cerebrospinal-fluid flow or establish clinical ventricular dimensions.

focuses.inspect: Rotate to compare spinous and transverse-process relationships. Each muscle set stays bilateral under the side filter; individual levels are not segmented or attachment-validated.

profiles.title: Back-muscle dissection
profiles.orientation: Start posteriorly and remove selected layers towards the smaller vertebral muscles. Psoas remains anterior unless a focused view excludes it.
limitations: Latissimus dorsi and multifidus are not supplied in this subset.
22 source-labelled whole discs are available; the remaining disc level is unresolved. Spinal ligaments, meninges and spinal nerves are absent.
The central-canal mesh is not the spinal cord; no laminectomy is simulated.

stages.title: Assembled anatomy
stages.description: All available structures in this region are restored to their registered positions.
stages.inspect: Rotate first. Notice which structures cover the others before removing a layer.

stages.title: Remove trapezius parts
stages.description: Remove the supplied ascending, transverse and descending trapezius parts.
stages.inspect: Inspect the remaining back-muscle envelope.

stages.title: Expose the longitudinal columns
stages.description: Also remove splenius and serratus posterior.
stages.inspect: Compare the longitudinal erector-spinae columns.

stages.title: Expose smaller deep muscles
stages.description: Also remove the erector-spinae columns and semispinalis.
stages.inspect: Inspect the remaining short muscles. The absent multifidus layer is not implied.

stages.title: Skeletal framework
stages.description: Hide soft tissues to inspect the available bones. Joint surfaces remain source geometry, not a simulated joint.
stages.inspect: Use the remaining bones as orientation landmarks, then step back to restore the preceding view.

stages.title: Central-canal reference only
stages.description: Hide bones and muscles to expose the narrow source-labelled central canal.
stages.inspect: This is not a spinal-cord segmentation and must not be used to infer cord thickness or boundaries.

stages.title: Connective-tissue relationships
stages.description: Inspect the available discs, cartilages, ligaments, membranes or tendons with their bony context. This is not a complete joint dissection.
stages.inspect: Check the available surfaces and their neighbouring bones. Most capsules, fascia, tendons and ligaments are still missing.

stages.title: Intervertebral disc column
stages.description: Remove the muscles and central canal to compare the 22 available whole discs with the vertebrae.
stages.inspect: Disc shells do not expose nucleus, annulus or endplates. The unresolved source disc is intentionally absent; source names are not validated radiology level labels.

stages.title: Deep cervical muscle sets
stages.description: A close cervical window with interspinal and anterior/posterior intertransverse sets. The remaining column and skull are excluded.
stages.inspect: Rotate to compare spinous and transverse-process relationships. Each muscle set stays bilateral under the side filter; individual levels are not segmented or attachment-validated.

stages.title: Deep lumbar muscle sets
stages.description: Compare lumbar interspinal and existing intertransverse groups within a lumbar-only skeletal frame.
stages.inspect: Hide a vertebra to inspect the small muscles. Source groups are not individual level assignments; the central canal is not included and no complete spinal cord is implied.

focuses.title: Deep cervical muscle sets
focuses.description: A close cervical window with interspinal and anterior/posterior intertransverse sets. The remaining column and skull are excluded.
focuses.inspect: Rotate to compare spinous and transverse-process relationships. Each muscle set stays bilateral under the side filter; individual levels are not segmented or attachment-validated.

focuses.title: Deep lumbar muscle sets

focuses.title: Short rib-elevator sets
focuses.description: Inspect the source-labelled breves with the thoracic bones available in this region; lungs and superficial muscles are set aside.
focuses.inspect: Use Thorax for the ribs and Spine & back for vertebral context. Individual rib attachments remain unvalidated. Longi alternatives are withheld rather than overlaid.
